NKE.rationale: Nike is in the midst of a painful multi-year turnaround under CEO Elliott Hill, but the evidence shows a business with deteriorating fundamentals and no near-term earnings recovery in sight. Q3 FY2026 (Feb 2026) showed EPS of $0.35, down 35% YoY from $0.54, with revenue essentially flat at $11.28B. Gross margins contracted to 40.2% due to ~300bps tariff headwinds in North America, and operating income collapsed to $650M from $844M a year prior. Cash generation has deteriorated sharply — operating cash flow fell to $430M from $1.79B in the year-ago quarter. The company guided for Q4 sales to decline 2-4% YoY and expects 20% China revenue declines, signaling the turnaround is not yet translating into top-line recovery. S&P Global revised its outlook to negative on April 17, and HSBC downgraded to Hold with a $48 target. The stock trades at ~29.5x diluted PE on depressed earnings, which is not cheap given the trajectory — PE has compressed from ~38x in early 2026 but remains elevated relative to the earnings power being delivered. Net margin has fallen to 4.8% from 9.4% a year ago, and ROE has dropped to 16% from 32%. While Nike retains brand strength (38% global athletic footwear market share, #1 among teens) and has $8.1B in liquidity, the near-term catalysts are negative: tariff headwinds persist through Q1 FY2027, China is structurally challenged by local competitors, and the dividend payout ratio has ballooned to 117% of quarterly earnings, raising cut risk. News sentiment is deeply negative (mean -0.19 over 90 days, with persistent -1.0 readings in April). The FIFA World Cup 2026 is a potential positive catalyst but is not yet reflected in guidance and the turnaround timeline extends to 2027+.
